alt: A gold dashed outline traces all four sides of an otherwise empty rectangle.
A rectangular region is completely covered by five rows of eight equal square tiles.
A horizontal gold segment spans the long side beneath a rectangle, with end marks.
A vertical gold segment spans the shorter side beside a rectangle, with end marks.
A four-sided shape has a small right-angle marker at each corner.
A square outline has right-angle marks and matching single tick marks on all four sides.
One filled square with four equal sides represents a single area tile.
A rectangular tiled region contains three rows of four equal squares.
A rectangle has one horizontal gold measuring segment and one vertical teal segment.
A rectangular object sits above a row of seven equal reference blocks.
A dashed gold path follows the four edges of a rectangle.
Four rows of five square tiles fill a rectangular region.
An empty gold-bordered rectangle appears beside a fully tiled square.
A six-by-six square and a ten-by-two rectangle use the same-sized tiles and highlighted outside edges.
A green rectangular yard is enclosed by a wooden fence along all four outside edges.
A red carpet roll is partly unrolled across the floor of an empty room.
A blank rectangular wooden picture frame stands on a workbench beside four trim strips.
A paint roller sits beside a rectangular wall with much of its surface painted teal.
Three partly unrolled sod rolls extend green grass across a patch of bare soil.
Purple ribbon forms a continuous border around a blank poster, with a matching ribbon spool nearby.
Square tiles cover part of a kitchen floor, with untiled ground and a stack of tiles beside them.
A string of round bulbs follows the visible roof edges of a small house.
A teal sheet partly covers a rectangular box top, with a matching paper roll beside it.
Five rows of eight square tiles form a yard with its outer boundary highlighted gold.
Forty equal square tiles completely fill an eight-column, five-row rectangle.
A rectangle has measuring segments along its horizontal and vertical directions.
One square tile appears beside a rectangle made from six tiles of exactly the same size.
Two tiled shapes have highlighted borders: a six-by-six square and a ten-by-two rectangle.
A six-by-six tiled square covers more space than a ten-by-two tiled rectangle at the same scale.
A seven-by-seven tiled square has its outside edges highlighted gold.
An eleven-by-one strip and an eight-by-four rectangle use matching tile sizes and gold outside borders.
